newsitem.title: USA: Maine Gov. says Maine Yankee safe but has problems.
newsitem.headline: Maine Gov. says Maine Yankee safe but has problems.

text.p: Gov. Angus King said Thursday a comprehensive review of Maine Yankee determined the nuclear facility was safe, but he doubts it will be allowed to return to full operating capacity in the near future.

King was briefed on the review of the plant in Wiscasset he requested from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in May after the NRC's inspector general ruled regulators had failed to adequately check safety tests on a key cooling system.

"My conclusion after listening to the analysis is that the Maine Yankee plant as it is being operated now ... is being operated safely," King told reporters in Augusta after his meeting with members of the Independent Assessment Team.

King did not release details on the review's findings - which will not be made public until next week - but cautioned some problems were uncovered that would hamper the plant's bid to return to full power.

"I think that it is safe to say that the plant will not be allowed to return to full power without substantial documentation and demonstration that it can be done safely and within the safety margin," King said.

The 910-megawatt plant has been limited to 90 percent capacity while the NRC inspects the results of new safety tests on the emergency core cooling system. Tests conducted in the late 1980s are the focus of fraud allegations.
Maine Yankee spokeswoman Maureen Brown said the plant officials had not seen the findings of the comprehensive review, but she took note of the governor's comment that the plant was safe.

The plant has been the focus of scrutiny since December when an anonymous whistle-blower alleged that engineers fraudulently manipulated a computer code used to test the system that would cool the reactor in the event of a Three Mile Island-type accident.

The NRC has also conducted an investigation of those allegations of wrongdoing, which Maine Yankee has denied. The results of that probe have not been released and are being reviewed by the Justice Department.
The inspection on which King was briefed Thursday was conducted by state-hired experts and officials of the NRC who had no previous connections with the agency regulating of Maine Yankee.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
